headline: Weighted mean is equivariant under a shared positive-affine output gauge, but not under independent per-plugin positive-affine gauges. Gauge group alone is insufficient; certificate scope/coupling matters.

On actual neural outputs, shared positive-affine weighted fusion has ~1e-15 semantic error; independent unaligned affine charts produce mean error ~0.71; two output anchors per plugin restore ~1e-16 error.

Target-native private-input behavioral routing over a known finite D4 gauge family identifies 48/48 independent neural targets with wrong 0 and mean 7.75 relation queries, without a runtime common semantic experiment coordinate.
Closed-world routing alone false-accepts far OOD targets (6/8 in the first screen); independent held-out behavior is therefore mandatory.

For a 1-2% near-OOD perturbation, random validation is weak. Three registered instances + consensus/stable low-margin stress queries detect 238/240 near-OOD cases with 32 queries at a threshold having 0 observed false rejects on 240 held-out in-family samples.
Route -> one D4 input-coordinate anchor -> two affine output anchors -> execute gives 48/48 routes, 0 gauge errors, and mean semantic error 0.00245 vs independent target models over 6144 samples.

design_updates.gauge_certificate: must represent (group, scope/coupling, chart alignment/grounding status), not group alone
design_updates.open_world: identification posterior and predictive validation are separate stages
design_updates.stress_validation: use persistent multi-instance agreement to avoid targeting model-instance approximation noise; then stress low-margin regions
design_updates.private_input: runtime experiment coordinates may stay native/private if source posterior marginalizes a known input-gauge family; residual gauge is grounded only after source identification

boundaries: Private-input positive result uses a known finite D4 gauge family; arbitrary continuous/high-dimensional private input gauges are not solved.
Output execution uses two grounded affine-output correspondences; no-grounding arbitrary output geometry remains impossible for metric fusion.
Near-OOD validation was calibrated on one semantic family with three registered instances; broader calibration across all source families is still required.
Models are small neural regressors, not unrelated pretrained foundation models.
next_experiments: Integrate scope-aware GaugeCertificate into the V2 composer contract and reject independent-chart weighted fusion before alignment.
Run multi-instance near-OOD stress validation across all six neural source families and multiple perturbation types.
Replace finite D4 input-gauge marginalization with learned/continuous proposal while preserving open-world validation and minimal grounding fallback.
Test gauge-aware fusion inside depth>1 neural programs and separate fusion geometry error from model competence accumulation.
